text: The 1-2 Patriots face a crucial Week 4 matchup against the undefeated Bills at Highmark Stadium, and all eyes are on Drake Maye as the young quarterback tries to reverse an early-season offensive collapse that has New England dead last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game. Maye insisted Wednesday that his right shoulder is "fine" and there's no issue with Mike Vrabel, but acknowledged his own decision-making has been the real problem—a point he reinforced after Sunday's 35-6 Jacksonville disaster, where he threw two interceptions and lost a fumble while calling both the offense's performance and his own play "unacceptable." The Patriots' offensive line situation grew worse this week when Greg Van Roten was placed on injured reserve with a thigh injury, though New England did add rookie OL Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad in hopes of shoring up the infrastructure around their struggling signal-caller. As the questions mount about whether the Patriots are even using Maye correctly offensively, Sunday's test against a 3-0 Bills team figures to be a defining moment for both the quarterback and the direction of this season.
